red-flags.title: Red flags before deeper research
red-flags.intro: Answer from primary sources. "Don't know yet" is a valid answer and tells you what to read first.

items.text: Has the auditor resigned or been changed in the last three years?
Does the auditor's report carry a qualification, emphasis of matter, or adverse remarks under CARO?
Are related-party transactions large relative to revenue or profit, or growing?
Have promoters pledged a meaningful share of their holding?
Is cash flow from operations persistently lower than reported profit?
Are receivables or inventory growing much faster than sales?
Are contingent liabilities large relative to net worth?
Is the company capitalising costs that peers expense?
Has there been frequent equity dilution or preferential allotment to promoters?
Have the CFO, company secretary or independent directors left abruptly?
Is there any regulatory order, penalty or investigation against the company or promoters?
Are disclosures thin, delayed, or inconsistent between filings and presentations?

forensic.title: Forensic accounting checks
forensic.intro: From the annual reports and notes, several years side by side. Ratios can be worked out on the Numbers tab, formula shown. A "yes" is a reason to read further, not a verdict.

items.text: Over five years, is cumulative cash from operations well below cumulative net profit?
Are receivable days rising, or receivables growing faster than revenue?
Are inventory days rising without a stated reason (new plant, stocking for a launch)?
Is other income a large or growing share of profit before tax?
Are interest or other expenses being capitalised, or is capital work-in-progress large and ageing?
Are related-party sales, purchases, loans or guarantees large relative to revenue or net worth?
Are there sizeable loans, advances or investments in group companies, or unexplained 'other' assets?
Are contingent liabilities large relative to net worth, or growing?
Did depreciation method, revenue recognition or other accounting policies change in a way that lifted profit?
Is tax actually paid (cash flow statement) persistently far below the tax charge in the profit and loss account?
On the Numbers tab, is the accruals ratio high, or the Beneish M-score above −1.78?
Do standalone and consolidated numbers tell different stories (profit in the parent, losses or debt in subsidiaries)?
